messages:
Sophia Patel: Thinking out loud — what if we introduce a lightweight "quota ambassador" that runs in edge proxies to do low-latency shaping and burst leases? Local leaky-bucket + periodic reconcile with central ledger. Pros: no cross-AZ hop on hot path. Cons: staleness/overcommit. Interested in tradeoffs and abuse vectors.

Tom Nguyen: I like the low-latency angle. Main worry is overcommit and abuse. If ambassadors can grant bursts independently, we need an escrow/lease model so central can claw back.

Devin Brooks: Quick sketch: ambassadors keep a local token pool. For larger bursts they request a short lease from central broker (e.g., TTL 200-1000ms). If broker unreachable, fall back to conservative local cap. That gives availability and safety.

Carla Mendez: Telemetry must be first-class. Ambassadors should emit events: lease_request, lease_granted, lease_denied, local_drop. That makes it possible to detect wide overcommit or weird spikes. Also require per-tenant attestation to prevent spoofing.

Priya Shah: Cross-edge fairness concern: a tenant could open connections across many edge nodes and multiply their burst. How do we avoid that? Global accounting still needed.

Sophia Patel: Hybrid idea: ambassadors use local counters for micro-second decisions and maintain a shadow sync with central that includes "available_credit" and "max_burst". Central issues periodic snapshots (every Xs) and short leases for burst windows; ambassadors accept negative acks from central to immediately reduce local allowance.

Tom Nguyen: API surface I'd imagine:
```
POST /lease/request
{ tenant_id, requested_tokens, window_ms }
200
{ granted_tokens, lease_id, expires_at }
```
Fallback: if no response in 100ms -> ambassador enforces local_limit = min(current_local_limit, conservative_burst).

Devin Brooks: Also include idempotency via lease_id + seq to avoid double-counting on reconnects. If a client retries, central checks lease state.

Carla Mendez: Security note: ambassador <-> broker traffic must be mTLS and signed. Snapshots could be HMAC'd with short-lived keys. Consider using the KMS rotation mechanics we already have.

Priya Shah: Abuse vectors I can think of: botnets distributing requests across edges; client-side header spoofing; connection churn to dodge per-connection smoothing. Need mitigations: global dedupe heuristics, connection fingerprinting, and friction for new keys.

Sophia Patel: Ops rollout suggestion: start in shadow mode (ambassador calculates actions but only logs). Phase to soft-enforce for 5% traffic, then expand. Provide rollback knob to central to reject all leases instantly. Also a migration playbook for tenants to opt into ambassador-aware budgets.

Tom Nguyen: Implementation notes: ambassador maintains a small in-memory map: { tenant -> { local_tokens, last_sync, pending_leases } }. Sync with central via streaming RPC or periodic delta. Keep state compact.

Devin Brooks: One more: fairness normalization. Central should periodically normalize per-tenant aggregate across edges and adjust future snapshots so large multipoint bursts are smoothed over minutes instead of seconds. That reduces headroom for churny abuse.

Carla Mendez: For observability: dashboard with per-tenant: global_credit, local_consumption, lease_denials, cross-edge_ratio. Alerts for cross-edge_ratio > 2x baseline.

Sophia Patel: Action items: 1) I'll draft an RFC outlining the ambassador model and the lease API; 2) Devin to prototype broker lease endpoint and client lib; 3) Carla to design telemetry events and dashboard; 4) Priya to enumerate primary abuse modes + detection rules.

Priya Shah: I'll list abuse modes and mock alerts by EOD Tue.

Tom Nguyen: I'll write a quick sim harness to show how leases + periodic snapshots behave under 100k tenants.

Devin Brooks: Prototype target: single-node broker + ambassador lib by next week. Will reuse existing token store proto.

Sophia Patel: Great. Ping me for RFC review. If nobody objects, I'll include a migration/rollback section and the rollout thresholds. :rocket:
